sections.title: The letter Zet
paragraphs: The letter name is (Zet) /tsɛt/. Its main sound is heard in (Zug) /tsuːk/, which means train. This letter has two sounds in German.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, press your tongue tip behind your upper teeth. Stop the air, then release it into a quick hiss. Keep your voice off. For the second sound, keep your tongue close to that same ridge. Push air through the narrow gap and turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: In almost all German words, this letter makes the sound in (Zimmer) /ˈtsɪmɐ/. In recent loanwords borrowed from English, it keeps the sound heard in (Zoom) /zuːm/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: Do not read this letter as a soft hiss like zoo in English. Put a crisp t sound before the s, exactly like the end of cats.
